title: Modulation of Phytochemical Profile and Antimicrobial Activity of Azadirachta indica Leaves by Drying Temperature
content: This study investigated the effect of convective drying (40, 50, and 60 °C) on the drying kinetics and the physicochemical, phytochemical, and antimicrobial properties of Azadirachta indica leaves for food industry applications. The Midilli model best described the drying behavior. Increasing the temperature significantly reduced drying time and raised effective diffusivity, with an activation energy of 79.3 kJ mol⁻¹. Drying sharply reduced moisture content (78.54% to 5.84%) and water activity (< 0.40), ensuring material stability for storage. Essential oil yield remained constant (5.67%), but higher temperatures enhanced recovery per unit of dry mass. Chromatographic analyses revealed that drying temperature modulated volatile and phenolic profiles, affecting bioactive compound stability and transformation. The essential oil exhibited selective antimicrobial activity, particularly against Staphylococcus aureus, demonstrating strong potential against foodborne pathogens. Lower susceptibility in Gram-negative bacteria was attributed to structural barriers limiting hydrophobic compound action. Overall, temperature control is key to balancing process efficiency and bioactive preservation, confirming A. indica leaves as a viable source of natural antimicrobials and functional ingredients for food preservation.
